key_insight: A multimodal cardiac foundation model pretrained on signals and textual interpretations from 1.7 million individuals can produce consistent, reliable cardiac assessments across hospital and at‑home devices and settings.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap caused by device and setting heterogeneity (hospital ECGs vs consumer wearables) and limited labeled data, enabling a single model to generalize robustly across clinical and home environments.
method: Large‑scale multimodal pretraining on heart signals paired with textual interpretations from ~1.7 million individuals to learn shared signal‑text representations.
Design for cross‑device generalization so the same foundation model can be applied to hospital ECGs and consumer/remote devices with minimal task‑specific tuning.
Extensive evaluation showing robustness and reliable outputs across different device types and real‑world settings.
impact: Provides a practical template for building robust, transferable clinical AI: reduces dependence on device‑specific labels, speeds deployment from hospital to consumer settings, and promotes reliable cardiac monitoring at scale.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: millions of heart signals + clinical text → multimodal foundation model → downstream cardiac tasks

paper_title: Cardiac health assessment across scenarios and devices using a multimodal foundation model pretrained on data from 1.7 million individuals
paper_authors: Xiao Gu, Wei Tang, Jinpei Han, Veer Sangha, Fenglin Liu
